summary: LLM token prices fell roughly 80% between 2025 and 2026, yet enterprise API bills continue to explode as usage scales—making inference-time optimization essential rather than optional. A combination of the five core levers (prompt caching, model routing, prompt compression, output length control, and monitoring) can realistically cut total API spend by 60-80% with no loss in output quality. Prompt caching alone is the highest-leverage, lowest-risk lever, reducing input token costs by up to 90% on repeated prefixes with structural (not quality-based) savings.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (prefix caching)
techniques.description: Stores the computed key-value tensors behind a repeated, static prompt prefix (system prompts, RAG knowledge bases, few-shot examples) so the model doesn't re-process identical tokens on every request. The saving is structural with no change to output quality. Order prompts so the static portion stays at the front and remains byte-identical.
techniques.savings: 41-90% reduction on cached input tokens (PwC found 41-80% API cost reduction and 13-31% better time-to-first-token)
techniques.example: Place your fixed 20,000-token RAG knowledge base and system instructions at the start of every request so the provider caches the prefix; only the user's unique question is billed at full rate. Avoid putting dynamic tool results inside the cached prefix, which can paradoxically increase latency.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Caches responses keyed by embedding similarity rather than exact match, so semantically equivalent queries (e.g. 'how do I reset my password' vs 'password reset help') return a stored answer without hitting the LLM at all. Best paired with prompt caching: prompt caching lowers the cost of tokens that always appear, while semantic caching eliminates entire requests.
techniques.savings: 30-50% of requests served from cache (typical 45% cache hit rate in production chatbots)
techniques.example: Use a vector store to embed incoming questions and, if cosine similarity to a cached query exceeds 0.95, return the cached response instead of calling the API—eliminating duplicate LLM calls for common FAQ-style traffic.

techniques.name: Model Routing / Tiered Model Selection
techniques.description: Routes each query to the cheapest model capable of handling it—sending simple tasks to budget-tier models and reserving flagship models for genuinely hard queries. Flagship models cost $2-3/M input and $10-15/M output, while budget tiers can be 16x cheaper for identical token counts.
techniques.example: Route 70% of traffic to GPT-4o-mini/GPT-3.5-class models, 25% to mid-tier, and 5% to a flagship model, using a lightweight classifier or heuristic to detect complex queries that need the top model.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduces the number of input tokens by removing redundancy—trimming verbose instructions, deduplicating context, summarizing long histories, and using token-efficient phrasing or tools like LLMLingua that prune low-information tokens while preserving meaning.
techniques.example: Run a long retrieved document through LLMLingua to compress it 3x before injection, or replace a 500-word verbose system prompt with a tight 150-word version that preserves all behavioral constraints.

techniques.name: Output Length Control
techniques.description: Constrains how many tokens the model generates, since output tokens cost 4-5x more than input tokens. Set max_tokens, request structured/JSON output, and instruct the model to be concise or return only the needed fields.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and add 'Respond in at most 3 bullet points, no preamble' to cut a rambling 600-token answer down to 150 tokens—directly reducing the most expensive part of the bill.

techniques.name: Batch Processing
techniques.description: Submits non-urgent requests through provider batch APIs that process asynchronously (typically within 24 hours) at a steep discount. Ideal for evaluations, bulk classification, data enrichment, and offline workloads.
techniques.example: Submit 100,000 overnight document-classification calls via OpenAI's Batch API to pay half the standard per-token rate for work that doesn't need a real-time response.

techniques.name: Monitoring & Cost Observability
techniques.description: Continuously tracks token usage, cost per feature/user, cache hit rates, and model distribution so you can spot regressions and prioritize optimization where spend is concentrated. You can't optimize what you can't measure.
techniques.savings: Enables 10-30% of additional savings by surfacing waste
techniques.example: Instrument every call through Helicone or Langfuse to see that 40% of spend comes from one feature using the flagship model, then route that feature to a cheaper tier.

techniques.name: Session Context Management
techniques.description: Manages conversation history in chat deployments by summarizing or truncating older turns instead of resending the full transcript each turn, preventing token counts from growing unbounded across a session.
techniques.savings: 30-60% reduction on multi-turn conversation input tokens
techniques.example: After 10 turns, replace the oldest messages with a 100-token running summary so each new request carries a compact context rather than the entire growing chat history.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library for LLM queries that stores responses and serves semantically similar requests from cache, supporting multiple vector stores and embedding backends.

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK that gives one OpenAI-compatible interface to 100+ models, with built-in model routing, fallbacks, caching, rate limiting, and spend tracking—ideal for implementing cost-based routing.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open-source; Enterprise plan from ~$250/month for SSO, support, and advanced governance

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform that logs requests, tracks cost/token usage per user and feature, and offers response caching via a one-line proxy.
tools.pricing_paid: Paid tiers from $20/month (Pro), usage-based scaling and enterprise plans available

tools.name: Redis Semantic Cache (RedisVL)
tools.description: Redis-based vector semantic caching for LLM responses with sub-millisecond lookups, supporting exact-match and similarity-based caching plus multi-tier strategies.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open-source Redis; Redis Cloud managed plans from ~$5/month scaling with usage

tools.name: LangChain / LangCache
tools.description: Framework with built-in LLM caching (in-memory, Redis, SQLite, semantic) plus abstractions for prompt management, routing, and context summarization.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open-source; LangSmith/LangGraph Platform paid plans from ~$39/user/month

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft open-source prompt compression toolkit that uses a small language model to prune low-information tokens, achieving up to 20x compression on long prompts with minimal quality loss.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.description: Open-source LLM engineering platform for tracing, cost tracking, prompt management, and evaluation, with detailed per-call token and spend analytics.
tools.pricing_paid: Free self-hosted and free cloud tier; Pro cloud from $59/month, enterprise plans available

tools.name: Bifrost (Maxim AI)
tools.description: High-performance LLM gateway offering semantic caching paired with provider-native prompt caching, model routing, and unified multi-provider access.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source core; managed/enterprise pricing via Maxim AI (contact sales)

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Routing marketplace providing a single API across hundreds of models with transparent per-model pricing, automatic fallbacks, and cost-based model selection.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-as-you-go passthrough pricing with a small routing fee on credits

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching by moving all static content (system prompt, RAG context, few-shot examples) to the front of every request so byte-identical prefixes get cached for up to 90% input savings.
Set max_tokens and add a 'be concise / no preamble' instruction to cut the expensive output tokens (which cost 4-5x input) by 20-50%.
Route simple and high-volume queries to a budget-tier model (e.g. GPT-4o-mini) and reserve flagship models for hard tasks—often a 16x cost difference for identical workloads.
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of repetitive FAQ/chatbot traffic to eliminate 30-50% of LLM calls entirely.
Move all non-urgent/offline work (evals, bulk classification, enrichment) to provider Batch APIs for an automatic 50% discount.
